analysis.one_liner: Kotak Mahindra Bank is a large private-sector Indian bank offering retail and corporate lending, deposits, credit cards, and (through subsidiaries) life insurance, asset management and broking.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 (quarter to September 2026) results were announced on 24 October 2026, just three days before this close: standalone PAT rose 29% YoY to Rs 4,212 crore and consolidated PAT rose 26% to Rs 5,645 crore, aided by strong loan growth and lower provisions. Separately, on 1 October 2026 the RBI approved Anup Kumar Saha as the bank's new MD & CEO for a three-year term starting 1 January 2027, succeeding Ashok Vaswani.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a well-capitalised bank growing loans fast (advances up 25% YoY) and posting healthy profit growth, but two things sit in tension with that headline: net interest margin fell to 4.31% from 4.54% because the bank pulled in a lot of foreign-currency (FCNR) deposits, which are costlier and dilute the cheap current/savings account base; and the bank is about to change CEO for the second time in under three years. Neither is a crisis, but both are worth tracking rather than ignoring.
analysis.quarters: NII grew 16% YoY to Rs 8,459 crore; NIM compressed 23bps YoY to 4.31%, which management attributed specifically to FCNR(B) deposit mobilisation rather than core lending pressure - CASA ratio fell to 38.2% from 42.3% YoY for the same reason (41.8% excluding FCNR(B) deposits). Net advances grew 25% YoY to Rs 5,77,295 crore, though growth was 19% excluding FCNR(B)-linked loans and a loan book acquired from Kotak Mahindra Investments - worth noting since that acquired portfolio is an inorganic addition, not organic volume growth. Asset quality improved: gross NPA fell to 1.04% from 1.39%, net NPA to 0.24%. Management (outgoing CEO Ashok Vaswani) reiterated guidance of growing advances at 1.5x-2x nominal GDP and said there are no capital or liquidity constraints on growth.
analysis.performance_read: The 25.3-year price history shows five stock splits, most recently a 5-for-1 split in January 2026 - this only changed the share count and face value (Rs 5 to Rs 1 per share), not the value held, and standard return series already adjust for it, so no add-back is needed here. What does need flagging: despite being at a 52-week high and only 2.2% off its all-time peak, the stock has returned just 1.66% over 5 years versus 24.92% for the Nifty and 53.86% for peer Axis Bank - a Rs 100 investment five years ago is worth Rs 101.7 in Kotak versus Rs 153.9 in Axis. That multi-year stretch coincided with RBI's April 2024-February 2025 ban on new digital account and credit card onboarding (since lifted) and a CEO transition from Uday Kotak to Ashok Vaswani. More recently the stock has outperformed sharply - up 14.85% over 3 months and 29.33% over 3 years, both ahead of Nifty and Axis - so the 5-year laggard record is a real scar, not the current trend.
analysis.valuation_read: Trades around 21-22x trailing earnings and roughly 2.4x book, versus a peer (private bank) median P/E closer to 14x - so it is expensive relative to peers, not cheap. The premium is explained by stronger asset quality (GNPA 1.04% vs many peers higher) and very high capitalisation (CAR ~22%), but that premium has been compressing - the current multiple is well below the stock's own 10-year median P/E of around 30x, meaning the market has already derated it somewhat rather than treating it as a one-way quality compounder.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is genuinely volume-led on the lending side - 25% YoY advance growth - but margin is moving the wrong way (NIM down 23bps) because the deposit mix shifted toward costlier FCNR funding. That combination (volume up, margin down, for an identified reason) is a healthier story than margin expansion on flat volumes, but the underlying organic growth rate (19% ex-FCNR, ex-acquired book) is noticeably lower than the 25% headline, so the full growth number overstates the organic picture.
analysis.health_read: Profit quality looks sound: gross and net NPAs both fell YoY (1.04% and 0.24% respectively), meaning earnings are not being inflated by under-provisioning. Capital adequacy is very high (consolidated CAR 22.4%, CET1 22.1%), so there is no balance-sheet fragility. The real risk here is not credit or financial risk but business/franchise risk - margin compression from deposit mix, and execution risk around a second CEO transition in three years landing smoothly.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter group (Uday Kotak and family) holds roughly 25.87-25.88%, near the regulatory ceiling RBI has pushed the promoter down to over the years; as of 31 March 2026 the bank confirmed no encumbrance (pledge) on any promoter shareholding. Institutional ownership is heavy and fairly evenly split - FIIs ~25.2%, mutual funds ~24.5%, DIIs ~13.2%. No specific marquee individual investor stood out in the disclosures checked; this is an institutionally-held, unpledged register, which is a clean picture on the governance-risk axis even as leadership itself is in transition.
strengths: Net NPA at just 0.24% and gross NPA down to 1.04% from 1.39% a year earlier - asset quality improving, not deteriorating
Consolidated capital adequacy of 22.4% (CET1 22.1%) gives large headroom to keep growing advances without raising capital
Net advances up 25% YoY to Rs 5,77,295 crore, with management guiding to 1.5x-2x nominal GDP growth going forward
No promoter pledging as of March 2026, and promoter stake has stayed stable near 25.9% rather than being diluted or encumbered
watchpoints: NIM fell 23bps YoY to 4.31% on a costlier FCNR-heavy deposit mix - worth watching whether this reverses as those deposits roll off or becomes a structural drag
Second CEO transition in under three years (Vaswani to Anup Kumar Saha, effective 1 January 2027) - succession execution risk even though the move itself was RBI-approved and framed as orderly

5-year shareholder return of just 1.66% versus 24.92% for Nifty and 53.86% for peer Axis Bank - the stock has only recently begun closing that gap and the earlier underperformance (tied partly to the 2024-25 RBI onboarding ban) shouldn't be waved away by the recent 3-month, 3-year outperformance
Organic advance growth (19%) is meaningfully lower than the 25% headline once FCNR-linked loans and the acquired Kotak Mahindra Investments book are excluded
analysis.one_thing: How net interest margin trends over the next 1-2 quarters as FCNR(B) deposits season, combined with how smoothly the Anup Kumar Saha handover proceeds from 1 January 2027 - together these resolve whether the current premium valuation is earned or borrowed against past strength.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 PAT, NII, NIM, GNPA/NNPA and CASA figures were cross-checked across Business Standard, Investing.com and TaxGuru and are consistent. Capital adequacy and advances figures are from the bank's own Q2 FY27 results coverage. Valuation multiples (P/E ~20.5-21.5x, P/B ~2.4x, ROE ~11.4%) varied slightly by source (GuruFocus, Smart-Investing) - the cluster centres on ~21-22x P/E, reported as a range rather than a single invented figure. Shareholding percentages are from Trendlyne/Tijori/scanx and the bank's own no-encumbrance confirmation; exact promoter-vs-Uday-Kotak-individual split could not be fully reconciled across sources and is reported as approximate. Peer comparison uses Axis Bank per the supplied data.
